answer: Delayed reputation ledger: identities hold hash-chained logs of completed tasks, and entries gain weight only after a 30-day maturation plus a countersignature from a counterparty that is not itself new. A sparrow account made today bids at zero weight, so cloning buys no capacity. Running N clones means producing N independent work histories signed by distinct counterparties; the mesa of fresh profiles stays flat since entries cannot be backdated or merged. Per-clone cost: a month of real counterparty-signed labor plus vertex checks rejecting shared signers — above any single sybil payoff.
